name: Nextdoor Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: Nextdoor (San Francisco; founded 2008 by Nirav Tolia) runs a verified-address neighborhood social network connecting residents with each other and with local businesses, monetized mainly through advertising [3]. Tolia returned as CEO, president and chair in 2024 after Sarah Friar stepped down [5]. Q2 2026 revenue was ~$75M (+15% YoY, above the $71-73M outlook), platform weekly active users hit a record 22.9M (+5%), self-serve revenue grew 32% to ~67% of revenue, net loss narrowed to $2M and Adjusted EBITDA was $10M (13% margin); full-year 2026 guidance was raised to low-teens revenue growth and ~10% Adjusted EBITDA margin [1]. Cash and marketable securities were ~$378M [1].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): The pivot toward self-serve advertising is working, with self-serve revenue up 32% YoY in Q2 2026 (accelerating from 28% in Q1) and now ~67% of revenue, but it is an extension of the existing ad model rather than a new business [1]. AI Deployment (2/2): Nextdoor ships generative AI to users and advertisers, including writing assistance for posts and AI-generated ad copy, and uses AI to moderate content and reduce hate speech [5][6]. Market Share (1/2): Platform WAU reached a record 22.9M (+5% YoY), rising sequentially for two quarters, but no share data against Facebook Groups or other local platforms was found [1]. Pipeline (1/2): Q3 2026 guidance is $76-78M revenue and $6.5-8M Adjusted EBITDA with continued WAU growth assumed, but no named next-generation products with dates [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D was $135M in FY2025, ~48% of revenue on a TTM basis, top-quartile for internet companies [4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Nextdoor's purpose of building trusted local neighborhoods is clear and distinctive to its verified-address model, and Tolia frames the turnaround around a 'Founder's Mentality' of owner thinking [5]. It is undercut by a long record of racial-profiling posts on the platform since 2015 and the 2020 removal of Black Lives Matter posts by volunteer moderators, which then-CEO Friar called 'really our fault' [7]. Community Impact (0/2): No quantified charitable or community-investment programs surfaced. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention data was found; Indeed reviewers (4.2/5, 72% CEO approval) cite a high number of layoffs, and Q1 2024 included workforce-reduction restructuring charges [5]. Insider Buying (0/2): The last open-market insider purchase was director Robert Hohman's 300,000 shares at ~$1.66-$1.69 in March 2025, outside the 12-month window [4].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock. Strengths: debt-to-equity of 6.7% (1.0) with ~$0.99 cash per share against a $2.30 price, TTM revenue growth of 9.8% (0.99) and an FY2020-FY2025 revenue CAGR of 15.9% (1.0, 2x weight) [4]. Weaknesses: ROE of -7.3% (0, 2x weight), net margin of -11.1% (0) and a negative forward P/E (FY2027 consensus EPS of -$0.037 implies ~-63x), which scores 0 [4]. Forward PEG is excluded because FMP's 0.44 figure is not meaningful on negative earnings. Weighted sum 3.99/8 = 4.99, rounded to 5. Liquidity (~$4.1M daily traded value) clears the $1M floor.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): Nextdoor's moat is a verified-address neighbor graph and hyperlocal user-generated content that AI cannot fabricate, and AI is a tool for its moderation and ad creation [5][6]. But its revenue is digital advertising and local recommendations, a category where AI assistants and AI-powered search can intercept 'who's a good plumber nearby' queries and where larger platforms deploy AI ad tools faster; research found no analyst commentary dismissing this exposure. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI features are shipping but no AI-attributed revenue is disclosed [6].

infinite_game.summary: Seen through Simon Sinek's lens, Nextdoor has the raw material of a Just Cause, neighbors who know and rely on each other, and its leaders have twice publicly owned failures (racial profiling, BLM post removals). But repeated layoffs, CEO turnover and a story now measured in Adjusted EBITDA margin points show a company still fighting for survival rather than playing to keep playing.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): The vision of a kinder, more connected neighborhood is distinctive, service-oriented and not fully achievable, and it shaped decisions such as ending the 'forward to police' feature in 2020 and adding anti-profiling friction to crime posts [7]. It has not yet been validated through decades of consistent execution.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership publicly accepted blame for moderation failures and changed policy, recruiting Black moderators and offering bias training, at the cost of friction in its most-used crime and safety content [7]. Tolia explicitly describes balancing quarterly pressure against reigniting innovation, but the current narrative still leads with margin improvement [5][1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The organization has gone through repeated workforce reductions (restructuring charges in Q1 2024) and a CEO transition from Friar back to Tolia, and employee reviews cite layoffs that left staff uneasy [5].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Nextdoor has re-founded itself under Tolia's 'third era' and shifted monetization toward self-serve local advertising (now ~67% of revenue), a meaningful but incremental evolution of the same platform [1][5].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found acknowledging competitors such as Facebook Groups or Reddit as rivals that sharpen the product [1][5].

investment_thesis: Nextdoor is inflecting: Q2 2026 revenue of ~$75M grew 15% and beat guidance, WAU hit a record 22.9M, self-serve revenue grew 32%, and Adjusted EBITDA swung to $10M (13% margin, +~$12M YoY), prompting a raised outlook of low-teens growth and ~10% EBITDA margin for 2026 [1]. With ~$378M of cash and securities against an ~$890M market cap and virtually no debt, the balance sheet gives the turnaround runway, and consensus models positive EPS by 2029 [1][4].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that Nextdoor remains GAAP-unprofitable (TTM net margin -11.1%, ROE -7.3%), stock-based compensation is ~22% of revenue, and WAU growth of 5% is modest for a social network [4][1]. Digital advertising is exposed to AI-driven search and assistants, and the platform carries reputational risk from racial-profiling and moderation controversies [7]. On the IOWN framework, weak Inspiration (2/10) and a FINITE Infinite Game score (4/10) hold the overall at 44, a WATCH.
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results against guidance of $76-78M revenue and $6.5-8M Adjusted EBITDA, with continued sequential WAU growth [1]
Self-serve advertising scaling (+32% YoY, ~67% of revenue), lifting revenue per user and margins toward the ~10% full-year Adjusted EBITDA target [1]
Path to GAAP profitability: Q2 2026 net loss narrowed to $2M from $15M; consensus shows positive EPS by 2029 [1][4]
key_risks: AI-driven search and assistants intercepting local-recommendation intent that drives Nextdoor's advertising value
Recurring content-moderation and racial-profiling controversies that could hurt user trust and advertiser demand [7]
Dilution: stock-based compensation at ~22% of revenue against a ~$2.30 share price [4]
